pr.title: Add the Release workflow: a version bump that merges tags the release (install.md chunk 2)
pr.head: 923a58f2baa4ba534ab6ab0e5dd177e3def35448

summary: Field is a command-line music production tool. Until this change it had no way to cut a release: package.json has said 0.1.0 since the start, and the repository has no tags and no GitHub releases. The install plan's one-line installer, a later chunk, needs a release channel to follow, so this pull request adds the release flow Projector uses.

1. Propose. A maintainer starts the Release workflow by hand on GitHub and chooses patch, minor, or major. Its propose job raises the version in package.json on a release/vX.Y.Z branch and opens a pull request.
  2. Merge. Merging that pull request is the decision to ship.
  3. Publish. The merge changes package.json on main, which runs the publish job. When the push raised the version and the new version has no tag, it tags vX.Y.Z, force-moves the major tag v0 to the same commit in the same atomic push, and creates a GitHub release with generated notes.

A release publishes no files. The daemon, field-audiod, links JUCE and the VST3 SDK, whose terms are copyleft (AGPLv3 and GPLv3) unless you hold commercial licenses for both. Publishing a prebuilt daemon would distribute it under those terms, so the plan now decides that whoever installs Field builds it. The release installer, chunk 3, will build from the tag's source.

Field's main starts at an untagged 0.1.0, which Projector's never did, so the publish job compares the version with the one main held before the push. A package.json edit that leaves the version alone releases nothing, even while 0.1.0 has no tag.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Immutable tag: vX.Y.Z, which names one release and never moves.
  • Major tag: v0, which every 0.x release moves to its own commit. The future installer follows it.
  • Propose job: the workflow job a maintainer starts by hand. It opens the release pull request.
  • Publish job: the job that runs on a package.json change to main. It tags and creates the GitHub release.
  • Exit 3: what node scripts/release.ts released returns when the version on main needs releasing.
  • BEFORE: the commit main held before the push, which the publish job passes to released --since.

cards.title: Repository settings the flow depends on
cards.html:
• Actions cannot open pull requests. can_approve_pull_request_reviews is false, so the propose job pushes its branch, fails, and prints the link that opens the pull request by hand.
  • One ruleset, on main only. No force push, linear history, squash merges, resolved threads, and no required checks.
  • No tag rules. Nothing stops the publish job from force-moving v0.
  • Private repository. Releases and tags are visible only to collaborators for now.

cards.title: Review history so far
cards.html:
• ec2aba7: changes requested. Two threads: any package.json edit before the first release would publish v0.1.0, and under a common pushInsteadOf setting the tests would push tags to the real repository.
  • 923a58f: clean. Both threads are fixed and resolved, the tags go in one atomic push, and the plan's goal line says Field can cut releases. One suggestion remains, on local tags after a refused push.

groups.title: The release script does each step, and works by hand
groups.kicker: scripts/release.ts and its tests: bump, set, released, and tag
intro: scripts/release.ts is a TypeScript file that Node 24 runs directly by stripping its types. It imports only Node's own modules, so it needs no pnpm install. It has four commands:

CommandWhat it does
bump patch|minor|majorRaises one part of the version, writes it to package.json, and prints it.
set X.Y.ZWrites an exact version. Both commands refuse a version that does not go up.
released [--since COMMIT]Exits 0 when the version on origin/main is tagged, and 3 when it is not. With --since, it also exits 0 when that version is not above the one at COMMIT.
tagTags that version, force-moves v0, pushes both tags in one atomic push, and creates the GitHub release. --no-release skips the release.
The version to tag comes from origin/main, never from your checkout, so a bump that has not merged cannot name a release.

The tests run the script against a temporary repository whose origin is the path of a bare repository on disk. The file clears every GIT_ environment variable and points git at no user or system config, so no rule in your own git config can send its pushes anywhere else. A stand-in that records its arguments replaces the GitHub release.

checks.text: Field's release version is package.json's alone. The daemon (native/audiod/src/version.h) and the model workers (DAEMON_VERSION in each worker's protocol.py) keep their own versions, which describe what each process speaks, so a release never touches them.

files.note: The four commands, released --since, and the tag step that pushes vX.Y.Z and force-moves v0 together.

checks.text: set compares versions as numbers, so it refuses 0.9.0 after 0.10.0. The test at src/release.test.ts line 76 covers it, and all 18 tests passed at this head.
merged fetches tags with --force, because every release moves v0, and a stale local copy of it would otherwise refuse the fetch.

This counts a local tag as released. tag creates both tags locally before it pushes, so after a refused push in a hand checkout, released reports the version released, and tag refuses it with "set a new version first", though the remote has neither tag. A CI re-run starts from a fresh clone and recovers, and the base head behaved the same. The review suggests deleting the local tags when the push fails, or asking the remote with git ls-remote --tags.

The GitHub repository comes from the remote's URL as configured, not from git remote get-url, which applies insteadOf rewrites. The test at src/release.test.ts line 184 checks that a rewritten remote still names its GitHub repository.
git and gh run through spawnSync with argument arrays, so no value passes through a shell.
One atomic push: a remote whose update hook refuses refs/tags/v0 receives neither tag, and a fresh clone then releases normally. The test at src/release.test.ts line 151 covers the same refusal.
--since releases nothing unless the version rose from the commit it names. A commit that cannot be resolved, such as an all-zero or empty BEFORE, exits 1 before anything is tagged.

files.note: Runs the script against a temporary repository whose origin is a bare repository's path.

checks.text: Every git process the file starts, the script's included, ignores the user's and the system's config and any GIT_DIR in the environment. The suite passed with pushInsteadOf rules for https://github.com/ and for / in ~/.gitconfig, in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/git/config, and in a GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL file, and with a stray GIT_DIR. Neither the decoy nor that repository received a ref.
This test guards the isolation above: drop the GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL line, and its pushInsteadOf rule for the temporary directory sends the push to the decoy, so the test fails.

groups.title: The Release workflow proposes a bump and publishes the merge
groups.kicker: .github/workflows/release.yml: a hand-started propose job, and a publish job on main
intro: The workflow has two jobs, and each runs scripts/release.ts under plain Node. The propose job runs when a maintainer starts the workflow by hand. It runs bump, commits the new version on a release/vX.Y.Z branch, force-pushes that branch, and opens the release pull request. The publish job runs on every push to main that changes package.json. It runs released --since with the commit main held before the push, and runs tag only when that exits 3: the push raised the version, and the new version has no tag.

This repository does not let GitHub Actions open pull requests (Settings > Actions > General > Workflow permissions). So today the propose job pushes the branch, fails, and prints the link that opens the pull request by hand. Merging that pull request still publishes the release.

checks.text: The workflow is Projector's release.yml step for step. It adds actions/setup-node for Node 24, the link it prints when it cannot open the pull request, and --since, because Projector's version was already tagged when its workflow landed and Field's 0.1.0 is not.
Every ${{ }} value reaches the shell through env:, never inline in a run step. bump is a choice input, and the script exits 2 on any other value. Both run steps pass bash -n after a YAML parse.

The organization's one ruleset covers only main: no force push, linear history, squash merges, resolved threads, and no required checks. No ruleset covers tags or release/*, so force-moving v0 and force-pushing the release branch are allowed. Both were read with gh api from the rulesets and effective-rules endpoints.

files.note: Two jobs: propose on a manual run, and publish on a package.json push to main.

checks.text: contents: write applies to both jobs, which push a branch or tags. Only the propose job adds pull-requests: write.
The force push replaces the workflow's own release branch when a run is retried. No ruleset covers release/*.

This step, run verbatim against a local bare remote in a fresh clone per push, with tag --no-release for tag: a script edit at untagged 0.1.0 released nothing, a bump to 0.2.0 tagged v0.2.0 and created v0, and a later script edit and a reverted raise released nothing. A re-run of the release run exited 0, and an all-zero, empty, or unfetched BEFORE exited 1 with no tags pushed.

groups.title: The plan decides a release is a tag that installers build
intro: The install plan had said a release would publish built files: a CLI tarball, a daemon for each platform, and checksums. It left open, in §7.1, whether a published daemon could carry JUCE's and the VST3 SDK's copyleft terms. This change decides §7.1: Field publishes no daemon binary. A user who builds the daemon for their own use distributes nothing, so those terms ask nothing of them. JUCE is not in the repository either, because CMake fetches it at build time.

Once every user needs a compiler for the daemon, a prebuilt CLI would save only the few seconds tsc takes, so the plan drops it too. A release becomes a tag and a GitHub release. The release installer, chunk 3, downloads the tag's source and runs the steps a checkout install runs.

checks.text: The plan stays in-progress, so the change makes no new readiness claim. The questions it opens go to chunk 3: how a release install links field (§3.2), and whether Windows gets an install.ps1 (§7.6). Which domain serves the installer (§7.4) and worker environments across versions (§7.5) stay open for chunks 3 and 4.

files.note: §3.1 describes tag-only releases, §3.2 builds from source, §7.1 and §7.3 are decided, and §9 records chunk 2 as built.

checks.text: §4's earlier decision, that releases ship built artifacts, is amended in place with what changed, as the repository's rules ask when new evidence overturns a decision.
This acceptance criterion holds at this head, while 0.1.0 has no tag: the publish step, run verbatim after a push that changed only a script in package.json, released nothing.
One obligation survives the decision: if audiofield.io ever runs the daemon for users, AGPLv3 §13 asks it to offer them the daemon's source.
§7.3 decides the case where binaries come later: build them on a maintainer's Mac, because a macOS runner costs ten times a Linux one under a $40 monthly Actions cap.
§9.1 records why the publish job compares versions: tagging 0.1.0 as a baseline would also stop the accidental release, but that tag would name a version nobody released.
can_approve_pull_request_reviews is false today, read with gh api repos/okamnesiac/field/actions/permissions/workflow.

groups.title: How a maintainer cuts a release
groups.kicker: docs/release.md, and the links to it from docs/README.md and AGENTS.md
intro: docs/release.md is the page a maintainer reads to cut a release: start the workflow, merge its pull request, and let the publish job tag it. It also shows the script commands for running the steps by hand, and says why the daemon's and the workers' versions do not move with a release.
docs/README.md and AGENTS.md each add the page to their list of docs. The AGENTS.md edit is in its docs list, outside the section that Projector generates.

files.note: The maintainer's how-to: the workflow, the script by hand, and the versions a release leaves alone.

checks.text: Matches the publish job at this head: only a merge that raises the version releases, and the verbatim run above showed it.
The version files it names exist: native/audiod/src/version.h, and DAEMON_VERSION in the aced and voiced workers' protocol.py. python/worker is the shared protocol library, not a worker.
